newsitem.title: SWEDEN: SWEDISH RIKSBANK STICKING TO INFLATION VIEW-RADIO.
newsitem.headline: SWEDISH RIKSBANK STICKING TO INFLATION VIEW-RADIO.

text.p: Sweden's central bank, the Riksbank, sees no reason to change its inflation estimates from its latest inflation report, national Swedish radio reported on Wednesday.
"Today there are no reasons to change the estimate," the Riksbank's chief economist Claes Berg told the news show Ekonomiekot.
In its June inflation report, the Riksbank expected an average annual inflation rate of about one percent in 1997 and around two percent in 1998.
The Riksbank targets inflation of two percent with an allowed deviation of one percentage point on either side.
In June, Swedish consumer prices rose 0.8 percent year-on-year.
